slides.title: Structural Patterns Overview
slides.prompt: Structural patterns explain how to assemble objects and classes into larger structures. Adapter bridges incompatible interfaces, Decorator dynamically adds behavior, Facade provides a simplified interface to a complex system, and Proxy controls access to an object.

slides.title: Facade Pattern Purpose

slides.title: Proxy Pattern Characteristics
slides.prompt: Which structural pattern acts as a surrogate or placeholder to control access to an underlying object?

slides.title: Decorator Delegation
slides.prompt: Fill in the attribute name typically used in a Decorator to hold a reference to the wrapped object.

slides.title: Adapter vs Decorator
slides.prompt: What distinguishes an Adapter pattern from a Decorator pattern?
options: Adapter changes the interface to match client expectations, whereas Decorator keeps the interface and adds functionality
Adapter adds new responsibilities dynamically, whereas Decorator alters method signatures
Adapter restricts access to an object, whereas Decorator optimizes memory consumption
Adapter creates families of objects, whereas Decorator manages database connections
slides.correctAnswer: Adapter changes the interface to match client expectations, whereas Decorator keeps the interface and adds functionality
